newsitem.title: FRANCE: European Parliament agrees unchanged 1997 budget.
newsitem.headline: European Parliament agrees unchanged 1997 budget.

text.p: The European Parliament in an unprecedented attempt at spending restraint agreed a European Union budget for 1997 which showed no growth in real terms.
The effort to contain EU spending is in line with the struggle by national governments to curb their own budgets ahead of Economic and Monetary Union, expected in 1999.

The budget was satisfactory because it respected the ceiling ministers had placed on EU spending, Irish Budget Minister Hugh Coveney said after the vote on Thursday, which finalised the 1997 EU budget.
Ireland holds the EU presidency until the end of 1996.
"The outcome is quite satisfactory from the (European) Commission's point of view," EU Budget Commissioner Erkki Liikanen told a news conference.
Overall, the Parliament agreed a 1997 budget worth 89.14 billion Ecus ($111 billion) in commitments, compared with 86.53 billion Ecus in 1996.

Euro-MPs agreed to a compromise with ministers on financing for European rail and road networks, European research and the peace process in Northern Ireland, for which they originally demanded 300 million Ecus.

The compromise involved using savings in other policies and drawing upon the EU's separate foreign policy budget to fund trans-European networks linking up with Central Europe and Mediterranean countries.
The battle over additional money for transport networks has been at the core of the Commission's plans to spur job creation.

But budget committee president Detlev Samland, a German Socialist, and Laurens Brinkhorst, the Dutch Liberal who steered the budget through the EU's directly-elected assembly, said they were disappointed at the failure to block Turkish aid.

The Parliament threatened in September to freeze all aid for Turkey, which MPs feel has reneged on promises to improve human rights and respect for democracy in return for the assembly's approval in December 1995 of an EU-Turkey customs union.
But in the end it agreed to freeze only the 53 million Ecus promised to Turkey for 1997 to help set up the customs union. This comes from a 1996-2000 package worth 375 million Ecus. ($1=.8015 Ecu)
